appearance_facts.fact: Large bold heading reads 'Reduced Screening Referrals Across Hospitals from 2012 to 2023'. A smaller gray subtitle below reads 'Referral-monitoring record shown in the dashboard summary'. The title's wording ('Reduced') conflicts with the line's overall upward movement.

A single orange line connects yearly points from 2012 (left) to 2023 (right). The line begins low (~1,200), rises with a mid-period dip in 2015, climbs steeply from 2020 to a peak at 2022, then dips slightly at 2023.
Y-axis labeled 'Screening referrals' with horizontal gridlines at 0, 800, 1600, 2400, 3200. The 2022 peak sits above the 3200 line; the 2023 point sits just above 3200.
X-axis labeled 'Year' with tick labels 2012 through 2023 in one-year increments.

printed_facts.fact: Years 2012–2023; the reporting period spans the full line. End value (2023, ~3,300) is substantially higher than start value (2012, ~1,200).
Title states 'Reduced Screening Referrals' which contradicts the plotted increase over the period.

public_definitions: Use the dashboard as the evidence source for selecting the appropriate screening referral follow-up pathway.
uncertain: The chart title says 'Reduced' while the data line clearly increases over the period; the intended pathway depends on whether the plotted values or the title wording governs the routing decision.
Exact point values are read off gridlines and are approximate (e.g., 2022 peak ~3,600, 2023 ~3,300).
